newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble lower as less money flows to T-bill market.
newsitem.headline: Rouble lower as less money flows to T-bill market.

text.p: The rouble eased in lively trading on Wednesday as operators transferred less money than recently from the currency market to the government bond market, dealers said.
Today the central bank is auctioning 7.5 trillion roubles of six-month T-bills and two trillion roubles of an additional tranche of a two-year OFZ interest-bearing bond.

"The market expected banks to seek roubles actively after transferring funds to the auctions but the supply of roubles has turned out to be plentiful and banks are investing them in dollars," one dealer said.
Another dealer said the rouble eased after a major government bond operator had stopped bidding for roubles.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,396-98 per dollar compared with an early 5,392-95 and 5,382-85 late on Tuesday. Tomorrow roubles dipped to 5,397-99 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,389-92.
The central bank said it had set 5,359-5,399 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Wednesday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 5-15 percent compared with Tuesday's late 5-10 percent.
